question.text: The equations of the lines <math><msub><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> are <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi></math> and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo></math> respectively. Suppose <math><msub><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> makes twice as large an angle with the horizontal (measured counterclockwise from the positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis) as does <math><msub><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi></math>, then the value of <math><mfrac><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mfrac></math> is equal to (where, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>)

solution.text:
Let, m=tan⁡2θ and n=tan⁡θ
And m=4n and m≠0,

∴tan⁡2θ≠0; θ≠0
tan⁡2θ=4tan⁡θ
2tan⁡θ1-tan2⁡θ=4tan⁡θ
∴1=2-2tan2⁡θ⇒2tan2⁡θ=1

⇒tan2⁡θ=12=n2
⇒m2=16n2=8⇒m2+4n2m2-6n2=105=2
